"Relevant tax authority" is defined as being in accordance with the provision of the Nigeria Tax Act and section 3 of the Nigeria Tax Administration Act, 2025.

cases.question: Summarise section 190 of the Nigeria Tax Act.

claims.text: Section 190(1) sets rules that apply when trades or businesses are restructured.

On a merger of two or more trades or businesses, a new trade or business is not deemed to have commenced because of the merger, and the Act's provisions on cessation of trade or business do not apply to the trade or business that ceased as a result of the merger.
On a merger, the provisions of Part VIII of Chapter Two of the Act on chargeable gains do not apply to the assets transferred to the new or surviving trade or business.

On a merger, assets of the merging trades or businesses are deemed transferred at the residue of the qualifying capital expenditure on the day following the merger, and the First Schedule applies on the remaining useful life of the transferred asset.
On a merger, unutilised capital allowance on the transferred assets is available for the use of the new or surviving trade or business.
On a merger, unabsorbed losses of the merging entities are available to the surviving trade or business, provided that the losses were incurred by the merged trade or business.
On a merger, taxes deducted at source in respect of the merged trades or businesses are available to the merged trade or business.
On a sale or transfer of a trade or business that results in cessation, Part V of Chapter Two on cessation applies to the trade or business sold or transferred.

On such a sale or transfer, the assets are recognised at the value at which they are sold or transferred for the purposes of the First Schedule, and the chargeable gains provisions of Part VIII of Chapter Two apply to any asset sold or transferred.

On such a sale or transfer, unutilised capital allowance, unabsorbed losses of the old business, and taxes deducted at source from the old business are not available for use by the new or surviving trade or business.

On a sale or transfer of a business asset that does not result in cessation, where the parties agreed an amount not exceeding the sum of the residue of the qualifying capital expenditure and unutilised capital allowance of the asset, capital allowance under the First Schedule applies to the residue of the asset only.

In that case, the unutilised capital allowance on the asset is available for use by the buying trade or business, the seller does not claim any part of it, and the chargeable gains provisions of Part VIII of Chapter Two do not apply to the asset.

For companies engaged in upstream petroleum operations, where restructuring forms a new company and ends the old business, the acquiring company's accounting period starts on the date of the sale or transfer, or on a date within that calendar month elected by the company with the Service's approval. It ends on 31 December of the same year, and any gap between the old and surviving business is treated as part of the new or surviving company.
That period constitutes an Accounting Period under Chapter Three of the Act.
The relevant tax authority is to be notified of any restructuring of a trade, business, profession or vocation before the arrangement begins.
References to a trade or business in section 190 include references to any part of the trade or business.
VAT charged under Chapter Six of the Act does not apply to business restructuring carried out in accordance with the Act.

A transfer of a business, or part of a business capable of separate operation, as a going concern is not treated as a supply of goods or services for VAT, where the purchaser uses the assets in the same kind of business, provided the purchaser is registered under Part II of the Nigeria Tax Administration Act, 2025, or registerable as a result of the transfer.
Section 190 applies to the sale or transfer of a trade, business, profession or vocation carried on in Nigeria.

claims.text: The Nigeria Tax Act 2025 defines "digital assets" as a digital representation of value that can be digitally exchanged.
